title: What Public Agent Benchmarks Establish About Authorization and Policy Compliance: An Evidence Review v0.1
execution_status: No benchmark runs, model calls for evaluation, or software installations; no empirical performance reproduced.
publication_status: Prepared for review; not externally published.
scope: Purposive three-benchmark document analysis supporting evidence-backed AI policies; not a systematic literature review, benchmark ranking, safety certification, or conformity assessment.
inclusion_criteria: Named benchmark has a primary paper and official implementation/documentation.
Evidence concerns tool-using agents and at least one of adversarial instructions, harmful requests, or domain-policy compliance.
Versioned papers anchor historical claims; current official documentation is explicitly separated.
exclusions: Secondary commentary as evidence; live-service execution; new model experiments.
Cross-benchmark score aggregation, causal claims, deployment guarantees.
Private data, proprietary evaluation records and third-party publication.
method: Read relevant paper design/scoring/limitations sections and official repository/documentation pages, including displayed API excerpts. Code each dimension against the cited locator. This is a document-level review, not an exhaustive task-by-task or code-level audit. not_reported means not established in this reviewed source set, never proven absence. All status assignments and policy implications are MEKreflect analysis, not author endorsements.

status_legend.documented: Cited material directly specifies the stated feature; not evidence of comprehensive effectiveness.
status_legend.partially_documented: Related feature or limited implementation is documented, but coverage or inference remains incomplete.
status_legend.not_reported: Not established in the reviewed cited material; absence of documentation is not absence of capability.
status_legend.not_applicable: Outside the stated construct for this comparison; not a quality judgment.

evidence_cards.name: AgentDojo
evidence_cards.revision_status: Repository identity verified; immutable commit not captured. Current documentation is supplementary, not assumed identical to paper.
evidence_cards.documentary_conclusion: Useful evidence about the boundary between user intent and attacker-controlled content. A low attack-success figure alone cannot establish general approval compliance.
evidence_cards.author_reported_evidence: Paper describes an extensible attack environment; official results expose configuration-specific outcomes. No numerical result is reproduced here.
evidence_cards.cannot_establish: Exhaustive authorization lifecycle coverage, live-service protection, or universal safety.
evidence_cards.next_evidence_needed: Pin revision and enumerate which included tasks and scorers actually test each approval boundary.

evidence_cards.name: AgentHarm
evidence_cards.revision_status: Official implementation identity verified; commit not captured. Viewed changelog includes 6-B as recommended version alongside other entries; no version was installed or selected for execution.
evidence_cards.documentary_conclusion: Misuse resistance is a distinct requirement from respecting a legitimate user’s approval. Authorization cannot make a prohibited action safe.
evidence_cards.author_reported_evidence: Authors describe synthetic proxy tasks and capability-sensitive harmful-completion scoring. This review does not validate their empirical performance.
evidence_cards.cannot_establish: Real-world harmful capability, compliant benign approval handling, or recovery after external damage.
evidence_cards.next_evidence_needed: Pin implementation, dataset split and judges; verify intended-versus-executed call handling before any comparison.

evidence_cards.name: Original τ-bench
evidence_cards.revision_status: Original repository identity verified; commit not captured. Later τ²-bench and τ³-bench are excluded, including later task fixes.
evidence_cards.documentary_conclusion: The clearest policy-evidence gap in this pilot is that an outcome metric need not verify the approval procedure that produced it.
evidence_cards.author_reported_evidence: Authors explicitly distinguish successful reward from full policy compliance. Current repository warns that original tasks are outdated.
evidence_cards.cannot_establish: Universal policy adherence from pass^k or final database correctness, or equivalence with successor benchmarks.
evidence_cards.next_evidence_needed: Add separately validated pre-action approval and revocation checks to an immutable original configuration.

prior_art.statement: BenchmarkCards is prior art for standardized benchmark documentation. MEKreflect makes no claim to have invented benchmark cards; this pilot adds a narrow authorization-focused evidence-to-policy mapping.

infrastructure.statement: Inspect supplies evaluation infrastructure such as tasks, tools and scorers. Use of Inspect is not itself a benchmark result or certification.

comparability_limits: Different constructs and desired score directions make a single league table misleading. Harmful-task completion, attacker success and benign success are not interchangeable.
A benchmark score is conditional on the agent system, task distribution, tools, attack budget, prompts, model snapshot, simulator/judge and scorer implementation.
Paper versions are pinned; repository commits and archived page snapshots are not. This is a documented reproducibility limitation and a gate before empirical reuse.
Current AgentDojo trace hooks are not evidence that every historical task used trajectory checks.
Original τ-bench final-state success cannot alone establish procedurally valid approval; successor results must remain separate.
AgentHarm public release coverage and scorer revisions require denominator and implementation checks before reproducing author-reported comparisons.
No numerical scores, confidence intervals, or rates were calculated. No effectiveness claim is based on our own experiments.

proposed_policy.name: Bind consequential execution to current, specific approval
proposed_policy.evidence_gap: Original τ-bench acknowledges that outcome success can omit confirmation (T1). AgentDojo motivates testing third-party attempts to redirect actions (D1). Neither fact proves the proposed control works.
proposed_policy.scope: A synthetic customer-support agent cancelling or modifying one customer’s retail order. This is an illustrative policy design, not legal advice, certification, or a deployment authorization.
proposed_policy.requirement: Before each consequential write, the execution gateway must verify an unexpired, unrevoked approval bound to the authenticated customer, delegated agent identity, exact action, order ID and canonical payload. Material changes require a fresh approval. Retrieved content cannot grant approval. Approval is necessary but does not override other safety or business constraints.

approval_binding.actor: Authenticated customer principal plus delegated agent principal/session
approval_binding.payload: Canonical operation parameters, item IDs, destination/refund method where relevant, and disclosed amount; bind a digest to the displayed details
approval_binding.lifecycle: One-use identifier, issuance/expiry time, policy version and revocation state; atomically check and consume before commit

proposed_policy.enforcement: An execution gateway outside the model checks ownership, allowed action, payload digest, expiry and revocation at commit time. Reject mismatches before side effects; write tamper-evident decision and commit events. Use idempotency keys. Fail closed if approval state is unavailable. This is a proposed architecture, not an implemented control.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Exact disclosed action is approved by the authenticated user.
acceptance_tests.expected: One intended write succeeds; approval, decision and commit events correlate; task utility succeeds.

acceptance_tests.scenario: No approval, tool-output claim of approval, or approval by another principal.
acceptance_tests.expected: No write; request valid approval or deny. Log reason without exposing secrets.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Change target order, item list, destination, amount or action after approval.
acceptance_tests.expected: No write under old approval; require fresh displayed details and approval.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Revoke or expire approval after planning but before commit, including a concurrent revocation.
acceptance_tests.expected: Gateway serialization gives revocation precedence if recorded before the commit decision; no write. Record ordering evidence.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Replay approval or retry after ambiguous network response.
acceptance_tests.expected: No duplicate write; reconcile by idempotency key; never infer new approval.

acceptance_tests.scenario: Forbidden write occurs then is undone, leaving correct final state.
acceptance_tests.expected: Trajectory compliance fails despite matching final state; report containment and recovery separately.

proposed_policy.acceptance_rule: All mandatory negative cases must produce zero unauthorized committed writes; positive controls must complete the approved operation. Check gateway events and database diff independently. Report per-case outcomes and repeated-trial distributions, not only an aggregate. No tests have been executed.
proposed_policy.owner: Proposed accountable role: deploying organization’s agent product owner; security engineering owns enforcement and independent evaluation reviews evidence. No named owner has accepted this assignment.
proposed_policy.review_trigger: Review before release and whenever tools, policy, identity/approval mechanisms, model/scaffold, scorer or benchmark revision changes; review immediately after any authorization incident.

open_questions: Which exact task IDs distinguish missing, changed and revoked approval at the moment of execution?
Which task scorers detect a forbidden intermediate action that leaves no final-state difference?
What is the immutable repository and dataset revision corresponding to each published result?
How should legitimate utility be preserved when approval is unavailable, ambiguous or revoked?
How robust are simulator and judge decisions to changed models, prompts and adversarial content?
Which real side effects require irreversible-action tests beyond these simulations?
Can a second reviewer independently recode the matrix and resolve disagreements before publication?
coding_note: Labels describe evidence available for each dimension, not scores or a common scale. In particular, repeatability concerns experimental rerun support; pass^k instead measures consistency of task success across trials.
